title: My favorite e-reader just got a big update
author: David Pierce

recommendations.name: The Boox Palma 2 Pro
recommendations.blurb: My love for this smartphone-sized e-reader knows no bounds. (Okay, some bounds, but not many.) This new model is fascinating: it has a color screen, cell connection, pen input… it’s almost a phone? At $399, the price is moving in the wrong direction, but I am deeply curious about this thing.

recommendations.name: ChatGPT Atlas
recommendations.blurb: AI browsers are kind of a dime a dozen. It’s Chrome with a chatbot everywhere you look! But given the sheer size of ChatGPT, this one matters anyway; if anyone can make a real dent in the browser market right now, it’s OpenAI.

recommendations.name: Plants vs. Zombies: Replanted
recommendations.blurb: The good news: PvZ is back! The bad news: it doesn’t seem like anyone tried very hard with this reboot. The upshot, I guess: I’ve already played it a bunch and will be doing so for the foreseeable future.

recommendations.name: The Samsung Galaxy XR
recommendations.blurb: It’s the Vision Pro, but lighter and more comfortable and half the price. I’m not bullish on headsets as a genre right now, but that’s still a pretty good sales pitch ! As an entertainment device, Samsung might have something here.

recommendations.name: The Aura Ink
recommendations.blurb: It’s the Samsung Frame TV of digital picture frames: a 13.5-inch E Ink panel that hangs on your wall and apparently only needs to be charged every few months. Neat idea , and everyone I know who has Aura frames likes them, but the $499 price is tough to swallow.

recommendations.name: Bloom
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been experimenting with a bunch of Mac apps that make the whole system a little easier to navigate — TabTab is a recent favorite — and I really like this app’s improvements to Finder. It’s worth it for the file-renaming and image-resizing tools alone.

recommendations.name: A House of Dynamite
recommendations.blurb: Another for the “premise is maybe a little too real?” files, but everything I’m hearing about Kathryn Bigelow’s new brink-of-war Netflix thriller suggests it’s as gripping as you’d hope. This is first on my watch list this weekend.

recommendations.name: The Fujifilm X-T30 III
recommendations.blurb: Lotta new cameras this week, including from Leica and Lomography ! But I am a sucker for Fujifilm’s X series — the company’s just doing a great job of making filters and presets more accessible, and even finding smart ways to incorporate AI.

recommendations.name: Glamping
recommendations.blurb: A Tubi original movie, directed by and starring the winner of a platform-wide contest for new creators. It’s a horror movie about influencers, the trailer looks either legit-good or so-bad-it’s-good, and I love a campy horror flick. I’m weirdly excited about this.

recommendations.blurb: The phone: I’m on an iPhone 15 Pro Max at the moment, but considering upgrading to a 17.

recommendations.blurb: After setting up my NAS a few weeks ago, I moved from Google Photos to Immich , a self-hosted dupe which is nearly identical. The process of moving the photos over was painful, but now I own my own image server.

recommendations.name: Task
recommendations.blurb: Finished Task on HBO today. Incredibly well done, totally devastating in parts and uplifting in others.

recommendations.name: NotebookLM
recommendations.blurb: I recently discovered a use case that, in my opinion, fully justifies its existence: loading board game instructions into NotebookLM and utilizing it as both a guide and, more importantly, a judge during arguments.

recommendations.name: Enshittification
recommendations.blurb: Just finished reading Enshittification by Cory Doctorow this morning. Was an excellent read, and I would highly recommend.

recommendations.name: RayCue charger dock
recommendations.blurb: Just got this RayCue charger dock to add some functionalities to my Mac Mini M4. Waiting for NVMe SSD to add storage to my Mac.

recommendations.name: MD Vinyl
recommendations.blurb: Been enjoying MD Vinyl . It’s just a great looking app that focuses on albums. These apps tend to be a dime a dozen, but this one has my phone on standby more often.

recommendations.name: Ball x Pit
recommendations.blurb: Ball x Pit has taken over my life just like Balatro did once upon a time.

recommendations.name: Zen Browser
recommendations.blurb: Zen Browser recently got a great update that makes a lot of quality of life improvements, and generally over the last few months it has become fully capable of being my daily browser.

recommendations.name: 3DBotmaker
recommendations.blurb: I really enjoy little cars racing down some serious tracks. 3DBotmaker is a YouTube channel where they do some awesome racing, and they’re in the middle of the DRC-X right now. It’s beautifully filmed, some great commentary, and it’s all about the big air, baby.

recommendations.name: Make Some Noise
recommendations.blurb: The best thing I’ve found, somewhat surprisingly, is Dropout . (I wrote this before John told me he also loves Dropout, I swear.) I only recently became a subscriber, and its giant library of good-vibes comedy games turns out to be the perfect thing to watch a few minutes at a time.
